method: The track is read from one of three inputs: a GPX document, whose trkpt, wpt and rtept elements are taken in document order with their lat and lon attributes, a GeoJSON LineString given directly, wrapped in a Feature or in a FeatureCollection that holds exactly one line, or a plain list with one latitude, longitude pair per line separated by commas, spaces, tabs or semicolons, where a third elevation column is ignored. GeoJSON coordinates are read in the standard [longitude, latitude] order and every latitude must be within -90 to 90 and every longitude within -180 to 180. Simplification is Douglas-Peucker: the first and last point are always kept, the point farthest from the line joining them is found, and if that distance exceeds the tolerance the point is kept and the two halves are handled the same way, otherwise every point in that span is dropped. Distances are measured on an equirectangular projection centred on the track's mean latitude with an Earth radius of 6,371,008.8 m, which is accurate within a region and drifts for a track spanning continents, and the projection wraps longitude differences at the antimeridian. The result reports the kept and dropped counts, the reduction, the polyline length before and after simplification with the haversine formula, the largest offset of a dropped point, and the simplified track as six-decimal latitude/longitude pairs and as a GeoJSON feature, with a warning when the tolerance shortens the path by more than five percent. Tolerances must be greater than zero and at most 100 km, and a track above 20,000 points is refused. Everything runs in the browser without uploads or network access.

sources.title: Douglas & Peucker (1973), Algorithms for the reduction of the number of points required to represent a digitized line or its caricature, Cartographica 10(2): points farther than a tolerance from the chord are kept recursively.
RFC 7946, The GeoJSON Format: LineString coordinates are an array of positions in longitude, latitude order, and a Feature wraps a geometry with properties.
GPX 1.1 schema: track points are trkpt elements carrying decimal lat and lon attributes, alongside wpt waypoints and rtept route points.
